Experiments were conducted at the U.S. Air Force's Turbine Research Facility (TRF), a transient blow-down facility with a full-scale, high-speed, fully-cooled vane and rotor stage.
Measurements of pressure, temperature, and heat flux were taken at flow conditions non-dimensionally matched to actual engine operation.
The vane had angled, fan-shaped film cooling holes to provide width-wise coverage along the airfoil surface.
The experiments found that the tip flow and vane wake-rotor interaction resulted in noticeable heat flux variations over time on both the vane and shroud surfaces.
The Popp method was used to determine the adiabatic film cooling effectiveness and film-cooled heat transfer coefficients from the experimental data.
The time-resolved data analysis examined the high frequency events associated with the blade passage frequency on the vane and shroud surfaces.
For the vane stage, the film cooling effectiveness and heat transfer coefficients varied significantly across the vane surface due to the unsteady effects.
For the BOAS, the unsteady pressure and temperature variations also resulted in significant variations in heat flux over time.
The compound shaped film cooling holes on the vane provided higher overall effectiveness compared to the baseline holes.
The experiments provided important insights into the complex unsteady flow effects on film cooling in a high-speed, full-scale turbine stage.
The research aimed to improve the understanding of unsteady effects to enhance the design and performance of gas turbine engines.
The test facility was able to match the non-dimensional parameters of a real engine, including Mach number, Reynolds number, and temperature ratio.
The instrumentation included pressure transducers, thin-film temperature gauges, and heat flux gauges mounted on the vane and BOAS surfaces.
Time-resolved and time-averaged data reduction methods were used to analyze the experimental results.
The research was conducted by a Naval officer as part of his Master's thesis at the Air Force Institute of Technology.
